en.html:
Nahi.

Not like that.
That was not what it had been.

The vow we made that day—we had accepted each other. Each other's will. Both wills, Muramasa. Not his when it pleased you and yours when the blame arrived.

What a convenient arrangement I had almost made. His resolve: very precious. His responsibility: arre, leave that outside, poor fellow has suffered enough. As though I could take the man apart, keep the pieces I loved, and announce that the rest had nothing to do with him.

No. Accept his will, and I had to accept his guilt also.

Muramasa's killings were his crime.
And mine, of course.

Ours. Both of us.

What we had done by our own wills—that was our crime.

Pity for him, guilt of my own: neither gave me the right to wash only his hands clean. He had not asked for such kindness. It was the very thing he had refused.

Accept it. His will and his responsibility, the same as my own. No special exemption because hearing his name beside the crime hurt me.

Two of us. One warrior.

　彼の意思と責任を認めよう。

　私たちは二つで一騎の武者なのだから。

en.html:
Ichijou"Oi."
Muramasa"May I correct what I said?"
Ichijou"Hah?"
Muramasa"We killed them. Mido and I. Both of us chose it."
Ichijou"..."
Ichijou"What sort of answer is that... trying to wriggle out of responsibility?"
Muramasa"No. If you are asking Muramasa to answer for her crimes and responsibility, I am ready."
Ichijou"Then we can fight right here, is that what you're saying?"
Muramasa"Wanting that is your choice."
Ichijou"What?"
Muramasa"I will run, though."
Ichijou"Arre, you just said you'd ANSWER!"
Muramasa"This is my answer. I will not fight against you."
Muramasa"But... right now I cannot die. So I will run."
Ichijou"How bloody convenient. You killed all those people without asking about THEIR circumstances..."
Ichijou"Everything to suit yourself, haan? Doesn't that strike you as a little much?"
Muramasa"...It does. So you may kill me."
Muramasa"A tsurugi without a warrior against a complete warrior-and-armor pair—the outcome is clear. But... I will struggle."
Muramasa"Almost no chance of success, and still I will struggle to escape and live. Yes... just as the people we killed did, before they died."
Ichijou"..."
Ichijou"Why can't you die now?"
Muramasa"Something remains for me to do."
Ichijou"What?"
Muramasa"Give Kageaki Minato his own will back."
Ichijou"..."

Yes.

If I accepted his will—then his present state, I could not accept.

Now it truly had been taken from him.

The shape of his mind had been changed. Not by his own decision. Somebody outside had interfered.

I would bring it back. His freedom to choose for himself.

I had vowed to be his tsurugi, his other half. This was mine to do.
